case_name: Harmohan Senapati vs Smt. Kamala Kumari Senapati And Anr.
facts_of_case: Plaintiff, wife of defendant No. 1, was driven out of her husband's house after giving birth to a child. She then filed a suit for declaration that the marriage of defendant No. 1 with defendant No. 2 is null and void.

legal_principles.principle: A suit filed by a person who is not a party to the marriage sought to be declared null and void will not lie under Section 11.
legal_principles.held: Either party thereto clearly means either party to the marriage sought to be declared null and void.
cited_cases: Jokhan Prasad Shukla v. Lakshmi Devi, ILR (1973) 2 All 853
Lakshmi Ammal v. Ramaswami Naicker, AIR 1960 Mad 6

legal_principles.principle: A petition for the annulment of second marriage under Section 11 can be presented only by the husband or his second wife, who were the parties to the marriage in question.
legal_principles.held: The first wife, who is not a party to the second marriage, is not entitled to present such petition under the Act.
cited_cases: Kedar Nath Gupta v. Sm. Supraya, AIR 1963 Pat 311
Amarlal Goru v. Vijayabai, AIR 1959 Madh Pra 400

outcome.final_order: The trial court's decision was confirmed, declaring the marriage of defendant No. 1 with defendant No. 2 as null and void.

use_for_drafting: drafting a petition for divorce under Hindu Marriage Act
advising on grounds of nullity of marriage
